the-wind-that-shakes-the-barley-2006.gazette: The Anglo-Irish Treaty of 1921 gave Ireland a Free State and an oath to the Crown, and men who had fought the Black and Tans side by side took opposite positions on it within months. Loach stages that debate close to the terms in which it was actually argued, in the same Cork countryside where the flying columns operated. The war that follows is between brothers who agreed about everything until they were asked to sign.

che-part-one-2008.gazette: Guevara trained as a doctor in Buenos Aires and arrived in Cuba aboard the Granma as the column's medic; the film follows the record from that landing through the taking of Santa Clara. It stages the literacy lessons the guerrillas ran in the Sierra Maestra alongside the ambushes, treating both as parts of the same campaign. The whole of it is cut against his 1964 appearance at the United Nations, shot in black and white.

red-cliff-2008.gazette: The battle was fought in the winter of 208, and the earliest account of it — Chen Shou's Records of the Three Kingdoms — amounts to a few terse passages about a fleet burned on the Yangtze. Everything after that is a millennium of accretion, and Woo works from both, staging the chained ships and the fire attack while keeping the commanders' strategy nearer the chronicle than the novel usually allows. The alliance holds for exactly as long as the wind does.
red-cliff-2008.prism: The chronicle is thin and the novel is thick, so any film about Red Cliffs is really choosing which one it means to be faithful to. Woo takes the chronicle for the tactics and the novel for the faces, which is why the strategy scans as history and the heroes scan as legend.

the-hurt-locker-2008.gazette: Mark Boal wrote the script after embedding with an American bomb-disposal unit in Iraq, and working EOD technicians have been arguing with its procedure ever since. Their objections are specific: real teams do not send a man down the wire alone, and the robot goes first far more often than it does on screen. The suit, at least, is the actual article — armor heavy enough to be its own hazard in the heat.

waltz-with-bashir-2008.gazette: Phalangist militiamen entered the Sabra and Shatila camps in Beirut in September 1982 while Israeli forces held the perimeter and fired flares over the district; Israel's own Kahan Commission later found the army indirectly responsible. Folman animates his way back through his memory of that week, interview by interview, until the animation stops. The last shot is not drawn at all — it is newsreel from inside the camps.

polytechnique-2009.gazette: On 6 December 1989 a gunman walked into the École Polytechnique in Montreal, ordered the men out of a classroom, and killed fourteen women. He left behind a typed letter blaming feminists for his failures, which police withheld for nearly a year before it was published. Villeneuve shoots the day in black and white and puts that letter on the soundtrack in the killer's own words — the decision that drew the loudest objections in Quebec before anyone had seen the film.
polytechnique-2009.prism: Reading the letter aloud puts his account of himself into the film unopposed, in his own sentences. Villeneuve's counterweight is structural rather than argued: the film keeps returning to the ordinary morning the letter interrupted, so the manifesto has to compete with it.

nostalgia-for-the-light-2010.gazette: The Atacama is dry enough that astronomers put their largest telescopes there, and dry enough that a body left in it does not decay. Guzmán films both uses of the same ground: the observatories up on the ridge, and the women of Calama crossing the flats with small shovels, looking for the remains of relatives taken under Pinochet. Chacabuco, a nitrate town abandoned in the 1930s, was reopened in 1973 as a camp.

heat-1995.gazette: The story came from a real Chicago detective's pursuit of a thief named Neil McCauley, and Mann drilled his cast with a former SAS soldier until the reloads were muscle memory. The downtown shootout is still shown in police and military courses for its sound and its trigger discipline; the actors move to cover the way the manuals say to. Two years after release, the men who shot up North Hollywood were reported to have studied it.

la-haine-1995.gazette: Kassovitz began writing on the day in 1993 that a teenager died in a Paris police station, shot at close range during questioning. He shot on a real estate at Chanteloup-les-Vignes, cast locally, and worked in black and white so the housing blocks would read as document rather than backdrop. When the film reached Cannes, French police officers turned their backs on the crew.
la-haine-1995.prism: Shooting on the actual estate is what gives the film its authority, and it is also the part that costs: the residents supplied the landscape, and the audience turned out to be Paris. A realism contract is usually signed by only one of the parties named in it.

maborosi-1995.gazette: Kore-eda came to his first fiction feature out of television documentary, and he shot it the way he had been shooting real people: camera fixed, at a distance, holding after the moment has passed. Half the film takes place in a fishing village on the Noto Peninsula, where the weather does most of the work the dialogue declines to do. The funeral procession along the shore is a single shot, held long enough that the figures become weather too.

vive-l-amour-1995.gazette: An empty Taipei apartment holds the whole film — three people drifting through it without any right to be there, at a moment when the city's property boom had left a great deal of finished floor space unsold. Tsai lets the camera hold and the rooms stay as vacant as they are. The last shot is a woman crying on a bench in a park still under construction, and it runs until the crying stops.

a-moment-of-innocence-1997.gazette: At seventeen Makhmalbaf stabbed a policeman while trying to take his gun, and went to prison under the Shah until the revolution let him out. Two decades later that policeman turned up at an open casting call for one of his films, and the two men agreed to restage the incident together, each coaching a teenager to play his younger self. The reenactment does not end the way the record does.
a-moment-of-innocence-1997.prism: Both men are directing their own younger selves, which makes the film less a reconstruction than a negotiation over what the day actually was. The policeman wants his youth back as romance and Makhmalbaf wants his as politics, and the freeze frame refuses to settle it, handing over bread and a flower instead of the knife.

green-fish-1997.gazette: Lee Chang-dong was a novelist before he was a director, and his first film takes a novelist's interest in one place at one moment: Ilsan, farmland outside Seoul that the government replaced with apartment towers in the early 1990s. The camera mostly waits — long takes, middle distance, no score doing the persuading. A man comes back from the army and the village is gone; what stands there instead has work for him.

titanic-1997.gazette: Before shooting, Cameron dived to the wreck itself, then had the ship rebuilt from Harland and Wolff's yard plans, deck by deck, so the geography of the sinking would be the real one. The film keeps to the actual timeline of that night — the boats leaving half-empty, the band, the two hours and forty minutes between the ice and the water closing over the stern. It also keeps the arithmetic of who lived: the further down a passenger was berthed, the less likely they were to reach the deck at all.

saving-private-ryan-1998.gazette: The Omaha landing was shot on an Irish beach with Irish Army reservists, a stripped shutter angle, and a retired Marine captain who put the cast through boot camp first. The wounds were built from medical advice rather than movie convention — arterial spray, men calling for their mothers, equipment lost in the surf before the ramp drops. After release, the Department of Veterans Affairs opened a hotline for veterans the sequence had sent back.
saving-private-ryan-1998.prism: The fidelity is the argument: get the wounds right and the opening stops being a battle scene and starts being evidence. The cost is that everything after the beach has to be a movie, and the film knows it — which is why the rest keeps reaching for a mission large enough to carry the weight the landing already set down.
